b: MILWAUKEE — On Nov. 16-18, 2026, the International Association of Exhibitions & Events® (IAEE) brought Expo! Expo! IAEE’s Annual Meeting & Exhibition to “Brew City’s” Baird Center.
Event professionals gathered for three days of education and connection-building, and enjoyed the can’t-miss show’s numerous cutting-edge opportunities.

“Expo! Expo! 2026 gave attendees a chance to step away from their day-to-day work, have some fun and experience Milwaukee together,” Marsha Flanagan, M.Ed., CEM, IAEE’s President and CEO, said. “I left inspired by how openly organizers, exhibitors, venues and suppliers shared what’s working and what they’re still figuring out. Bringing the industry together gives attendees a chance to hear how others are tackling the same challenges and see their own work from a different perspective. For me, the real measure of Expo! Expo! is how the experience helps attendees grow personally and professionally, and what they take back to their teams and put to work on their next event.”
Learn about Expo! Expo! 2026’s major takeaways and memorable moments in Trade Show Executive’s (TSE) digital recap.
For the first time, IAEE offered satellite registration at the event’s main hotels and its Opening Party at the Harley-Davidson Museum.
At the Opening Party, attendees set the tone for a productive, energetic week and explored artifacts from one of the U.S.’ most memorable brands. The IAEE/TSNN Awards were presented as well.
IAEE held the Expo! Expo! Opening Party at the Harley-Davidson Museum.
November 17 began with the General Session and 2026 CEM presentation in the Baird Center’s Baird Ballroom.
“This week is about connection, learning from one another, celebrating what makes this industry so special, and strengthening the relationships that move all of us forward,” Flanagan told attendees.
Flanagan and Brian Pagel, IAEE’s 2026 Chair and Chief Revenue Officer at SEMA/PRI, also encouraged attendees to take a “Maverick Minute” for safety.

Pagel presented the 2026 Chairperson Award to Beth Cowperthwaite, a former colleague of his at Emerald (which is now part of Forge). Pagel emphasized Cowperthwaite’s meaningful impact on his journey, which includes her coordination of his December 2025 TSE Power Lunch photo shoot and interview.

“Beth, you’ve been more than a former colleague,” Pagel said. “You’re a trusted advisor, a champion and, most importantly, a true friend. I’m genuinely excited that I was able to navigate this year with you.”
Then, Milwaukee Mayor Cavalier Johnson welcomed attendees to the city.

Brian Pagel presented the 2026 Chairperson Award to Beth Cowperthwaite, a former colleague of his at Emerald (which is now part of Forge). Pictured left to right: Marsha Flanagan, Cowperthwaite and Pagel.

“Milwaukee is a city built on bringing people together,” Johnson said. “We’re a city of industry, innovation, entrepreneurship, culture and creativity, and just like the exhibitions and events industry, we understand the power of partnership and bringing people together to build new relationships, showcase innovation and create new opportunities for the people that call our city home.”
Next, it was time for the 2026 CEM presentation. IAEE honored 37 CEM graduates, three CEM-AP graduates and one CEM Fellow Designation: Dan Cole.
Also, keynote speaker Cassandra Worthy of Change Enthusiasm® Global talked about the transformative power of change.

“When you can commit to getting one percent better every single day, the light that you shine in the world will get brighter. And when your light gets brighter, the people around you, their light will want to get brighter as well,” Worthy said.
Finally, Pagel handed the reins over to IAEE’s 2027 Chairperson: Michelle Edmonson, CEM, Vice President of Exhibitions at AMT – The Association For Manufacturing Technology.
Related. Manufacturing Momentum: TSE’s November 2026 Power Lunch with Michelle Edmonson, CEM

“I’m so excited to be here with all of you,” Edmonson said. “We have a lot going on in 2027, and just like we just heard Cassandra say, we have some changes coming up. We’ve brought in the EXHIBITOR Group [which IAEE acquired in 2026] and one of the biggest focuses is hearing them, hearing you and really understanding how our ecosystem can grow together and how everybody can feel like they belong. I’m really excited to get all of your insights to see how we can move this forward.”
Expo! Expo! 2026 introduced the IAEE + Exhibitor Experience.
Then, it was time for the show floor to open. The new IAEE Speedway, a race car simulator, got participants revved up throughout the week.

Also new in the Expo! Expo! exhibition hall was the IAEE + Exhibitor Experience, a collaborative learning environment for marketers, exhibitors and organizers. It incorporated expertise from EXHIBITOR Group and included the latest strategies in marketing, exhibiting, working effectively with event partners and sustainability.

Expo! Expo! also launched an Industry Collective where attendees visited with IAEE, Exhibitions & Conferences Alliance, Exhibition Services & Contractors Association, Experiential Designers & Producers Association, International Association of Venue Managers and Society of Independent Show Organizers.

Dedicated to C-Suite executives, the Innovation Lab showcased cutting-edge ideas, solutions and strategies, and examined the forces shaping the future of exhibitions and events. On November 17, attendees visited one-on-one with strategic thinkers from Events Venture Group.
The Tech Startup Central Pavilion highlighted the next-gen technologies that are shaping the future and connected startups with investors, industry leaders and potential partners.

Also, in the Sustainability Sanctuary, industry leaders, solution providers and advocates collaborated on real-world challenges, discovered innovative techniques and collectively drove positive change.

The show concluded with the Expo! Expo! 2027 New Orleans party at 3rd St Market Hall.
On November 17, event professionals had the option to participate in IAEE’s new Expo! Expo! Dine Around and Food Tours and explore some of Milwaukee’s finest restaurants.
IAEE hosted numerous other experiences that evening, including a Young Professionals Party and a Pride Party.
The show concluded with the Expo! Expo! 2027 New Orleans party at 3rd St Market Hall, which had a live jazz band.
Expo! Expo! 2027 is set for Dec. 6-8 in New Orleans.
